warnings: Quiz language appears sparse; make assessment prompts explicit.

improvement_notes: Remove the sentence beginning "An illustrator could show three panels" because the lesson already contains the corresponding visual; it reads like leftover production direction rather than published instruction.

Clarify that the inverse-square equation is a deliberately simplified classroom model and may not even approximate some short-range reflective modules; the existing caveat is good but could appear before the equation’s interpretation to prevent overgeneralization.

The phrase "feedback-related decision" is unnecessarily ambiguous. Say that a threshold action uses sensor-based feedback, while a single threshold trigger is not continuous regulation or closed-loop distance control.
Consider removing or explaining the sensor height detail in the worked robotics example. It is not used in the calculation and may distract beginners from the stated sensor-to-wall distance.

Add one compact note that some common IR modules estimate proximity indirectly through photodiode intensity, while others use triangulation or onboard signal processing. This would prevent students from assuming all IR sensors follow the same signal-distance behavior.

The lesson is strong but slightly long for a foundational sensor class. The repeated warnings about calibration, surface properties, and exact distance could be consolidated in one or two places without losing rigor.
In the optional noise extension, specify a reproducible disturbance range or example implementation so students can complete the activity without inventing the noise model themselves.
